ok.explanation: Peak power (80 kW) is reached at the **base speed of 3321 rpm**, not at redline. From base speed up to the 7000 rpm redline the motor holds ≈80 kW while torque falls off as 1/rpm. So **capping power at 80 kW does NOT cap rpm** — the motor still spins to 7000 rpm, it just can't make more than 80 kW doing it. RPM is limited by the motor's redline and your gear ratio, a separate thing from the power cap.
ok.note: 'Peak' vs 'continuous' is a thermal limit, not two power numbers. The FSAE rule caps tractive power at 80 kW — that's the ceiling. **Peak 80 kW** is what you may pull in short bursts; **continuous 56 kW** is what the motor+inverter can hold without overheating, and it is at or below peak — set by cooling, never above the cap. You cannot have 'peak 80 kW and a higher continuous'; continuous ≤ peak ≤ 80 kW always.

myths_default_wheel.claim: We must limit RPM (e.g. to ~7k) because motor power can't exceed 80 kW.
myths_default_wheel.correction: No — power and rpm are separate limits. The motor hits 80 kW at its base speed (~3321 rpm) and then holds that power all the way to the 7000 rpm redline. Limiting power does not lower the redline; the controller just stops torque rising past the point where T×ω = 80 kW. RPM is set by redline and gearing.

myths_default_wheel.claim: We can run peak 80 kW and also have a separate, higher continuous power.
myths_default_wheel.correction: Continuous power is always ≤ peak. The 80 kW FSAE cap is the ceiling for BOTH. 'Continuous' (~56 kW here) is what cooling lets you sustain; 'peak' (80 kW) is a short burst up to the cap. You raise continuous by cooling better, not by exceeding the cap.

myths_default_wheel.claim: Redline choice is about the power cap.
myths_default_wheel.correction: Redline (7000 rpm) with your 4.00:1 final drive sets top speed (~150 km/h), not the power cap. Pick redline/gearing for the speed range you need; the 80 kW cap is enforced separately by the controller.
